title: Veritas - Demystifying Silent Data Corruptions: uArch-Level Modeling and Fleet Data of Modern x86 CPUs
problem: Silent Data Corruptions (SDCs) caused by silicon defects in arithmetic units (integer and FP units) of modern x86 CPUs are poorly characterized at the microarchitecture level; no public data exists on SDC incident rates across CPU microarchitectures or workloads at fleet scale.
motivation: Hyperscalers report ~1-in-1000 defective CPU chips leading to SDCs; without microarchitecture-level fault models for arithmetic units, hardware and software protection mechanisms cannot be effectively targeted.
method: They used gem5 (a computer simulator) to deliberately inject faults into arithmetic units (integer and floating-point components) of five modern x86 processor designs, measuring how often these faults cause silent data corruptions—wrong results without crashes. The simulation tested different instruction classes and arithmetic unit types. They combined these results with real defect measurements from large-scale datacenters to estimate how often silent data corruptions actually occur in deployed systems.
key_novelty: This is the first detailed study of silent data corruptions in arithmetic units (the math-doing parts, not memory) across five x86 processor designs, using real defect data from datacenters to estimate actual occurrence rates.
contributions: First systematic uArch-level fault modeling of integer and floating-point arithmetic units in modern x86 CPUs.
SDC probability and rate characterization across five x86 microarchitectures, arithmetic unit types, and instruction classes.
Integration of real-world datacenter defect rates with gem5 simulation to estimate SDC incident rates at fleet scale.
Actionable insights for hardware-based and software-based fault protection targeting the highest-risk arithmetic units and workloads.

metrics.other: SDC probability and incident rates quantified across 5 x86 microarchitectures; integrated with 1-in-1000 fleet defect rate

baselines: Prior work on DRAM/cache array fault effects (not arithmetic units)
limitations: Fault injection is simulation-based (gem5); validation against actual silicon-defect-induced SDC events at fleet scale is limited by access to proprietary hardware data.
primary_theme: Microarchitecture-level modeling of silent data corruptions in x86 arithmetic units
